description: T-SQL relational storage and stored-procedure contracts for SQL Server 2019, SQL Server 2022 and Azure SQL Database.

supports.description: One schema.sql per component for the storage records it owns: schema-qualified tables with exact column types, lengths, precision, scale, collation and nullability. Each file creates the schemas it uses idempotently, and a foreign key into another component's table needs that component's file applied first.
Primary key, unique constraints, foreign keys with delete action, check constraints from expression predicates, and indexes.
Stored-procedure parameter and result-set contract, positional parameter order, declared writes and transaction scope.
Execution of an authored migration script against representative fixture data.

One contract-tests.sql per component checks the deployed catalog for exact column types, collation and nullability, the primary key, unique keys, foreign keys, check constraints, indexes, defaults and identity, without depending on constraint names.

unsupported.reason: Views are not represented by a storage record.
Trigger behavior is not part of the declared contract.
System-versioned temporal tables are not represented.
A prose check predicate cannot be rendered as a CHECK constraint.
External schemas are not represented as a closed local type contract.

tooling.purpose: Builds generated DDL as a SQL database project against the target platform (Microsoft.Build.Sql).
Provides the disposable fixture database engine.
Executes generated DDL and contract tests in the fixture database.

proofLimits: A target-platform build proves syntax and object references under the selected platform, not runtime data, permissions or transactions.
Catalog conformance and behavioral execution in a disposable fixture establish the declared fixture claims, not equivalence to a deployed target.
Migration execution against representative fixture data does not establish behavior on production data volumes.

checks.claim: The generated DDL builds as a SQL database project for the target platform with every object reference resolved.
checks.limits: Target-platform build only; no data, permission or transaction behavior.

checks.claim: Every generated T-SQL file parses without error under ScriptDom for the selected platform.
checks.limits: Syntax only; no object reference, type or runtime behavior is checked.

checks.claim: After deployment to a disposable fixture database, the catalog's column types, widths, precision, scale, nullability, keys, constraints and routines match the storage and routine records.
checks.limits: Fixture catalog only; a deployed target is not inspected.

checks.claim: The generated contract tests pass against the conforming procedure fixture and fail against the violating fixture with the expected contract code.
checks.limits: Declared procedure contract subset in a fixture; unasserted business behavior and concurrency under load are not covered.

checks.claim: A failing statement inside a routine's declared transaction scope rolls back every write in that scope in the fixture database.
checks.limits: Single-session rollback in a fixture; isolation-level anomalies under concurrent load are not established.

checks.claim: Each declared migration script, applied to the previous storage shape loaded with representative rows, yields the new shape with the rows preserved or transformed as declared.
checks.limits: Representative fixture rows only; production volume, lock duration and availability are not measured.

checks.claim: The fixture database can be backed up and the backup verified, and every declared index exists after deployment.
checks.limits: Recovery of a fixture database only; workload performance and monitoring obligations of a deployed target are not established.
